contexts.text: Not from so lawful a bed.
That which is multiplied from marriage is lawful, thus true; but that which is from adultery is not lawful, but spurious, thus not true.
In order that illegitimate conjunction might become legitimate...
The legitimate causes of separation are those which follow. CL 252. CL 253. CL 254.
By legitimate causes are not here meant judicial causes; but such as are legitimate in regard to the other consort.
Not at all with those who from causes legitimate...
That concubinage apart from a wife, when it takes place from causes legitimate, just, and truly weighty, is not unlawful. General article.
That the legitimate causes of this concubinage are the legitimate causes of divorce, when the wife is nevertheless retained at home. General article.
